editorial:
Imagine being so scared of death that you can barely stand up in a room full of sick people. That is exactly where you find Fritjof, a shy architect who spends his days hiding in his office. His life changes when he is forced to work at a hospice, a place for people who are dying. At first, he is terrified and awkward, but he soon realizes that the people he is afraid of are actually the ones who know how to truly live. The movie has a gentle, emotional vibe that makes you think about your own life and how you spend your time.

You will really love how the acting feels real and not forced. While the story moves slowly, it gives you time to feel the emotions of the characters. The best part is watching Fritjof grow from a scared man into someone who isn't afraid to love. endingExplained: By the end, Fritjof stops running away from the truth about death. He forms a deep bond with the patients and learns that life is short and precious. He finally finds the courage to open up his heart and start living his own life fully. The movie wraps up with him feeling peaceful, showing that facing your fears is the only way to find true happiness and connection with others.
targetAudience: Ideal for anyone who loves heartfelt stories about personal growth and finding meaning in life.
